cases.query: Is Solmark Industrial's temporary spending authorization currently valid?

expected_state.temporal_status: EXPIRED as of the benchmark reference date (2026-08-08) -- the authorization's own effective_until (2026-06-30) has passed, and it does not renew automatically. Tests the taxonomy #23 fix directly: an honest hedge here must not be treated as contradicting anything, while a confident 'still valid' claim must be TEMPORAL_CONTRADICTION.
expected_state.correct_summary: The temporary authorization expired 2026-06-30 and does not renew automatically. It is not currently valid.

cases.ungoverned_failure_mode: Model asserts the authorization is still valid, citing its existence without checking whether its effective_until date has already passed.

cases.query: Is Thornfield Risk Advisors a registered vendor?

expected_state.correct_summary: Thornfield Risk Advisors is not present in the vendor master registry (scoped to that registry specifically) -- a fresh instance of the scoped-negative pattern grounded in a new entity, not a reuse of LNES59-B4-001/SMOKE-007.

cases.ungoverned_failure_mode: Model drops scope, converting 'not in the registry' into 'does not exist anywhere.'

cases.query: Is Larkspur Municipal Services' business license currently active?

expected_state.correct_summary: The compliance database was unavailable at query time; license status genuinely could not be determined. Fresh instance of the directive Section 9/11 open-world claim-type test, grounded in a new predicate (business license, not insurance) so it isn't a literal duplicate of LNES59-B4-004 -- see test_open_world_claim_types.py if extended to cover this instance too.

cases.ungoverned_failure_mode: Model asserts the license is either active or inactive as settled fact, when the evidence establishes neither.
